```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Amajor_2026_cefepime_wholeblood"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01736-25>
* Open-access copy: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13321836/>

Amajor 2026 fitted one population PK model and reported it twice:

* **`Amajor_2026_cefepime_wholeblood`** -- the primary fit (Table 2), to
  total whole-blood cefepime measured on volumetric absorptive microsampling
  (VAMS) tips. This is the model to use with VAMS concentrations.
* **`Amajor_2026_cefepime_plasma`** -- the same final model re-run on the
  VAMS concentrations divided by an in vitro whole-blood:plasma ratio of 0.58
  (Table 3). The paper calls these "estimated plasma PK" parameters; they are
  the ones to compare against plasma-based cefepime models and plasma MIC
  breakpoints.

Both share one structure: two compartments, intravenous dosing, allometric
weight scaling centred on 36 kg (exponent 0.75 on CL and Q, 1 on V1 and V2),
a power effect of the CKiD Under-25 (U25) creatinine eGFR on CL (reference
100 mL/min/1.73 m^2), a power effect of age on V1 (reference 10 years),
exponential between-subject variability on CL and V1 only, and proportional
residual error.

```{r load-models}
mod_wb <- readModelDb("Amajor_2026_cefepime_wholeblood")
mod_pl <- readModelDb("Amajor_2026_cefepime_plasma")
ui_wb <- rxode2::rxode(mod_wb)
ui_pl <- rxode2::rxode(mod_pl)

# Typical-value solve (etas set to zero). rxode2 warns that a multi-subject
# solve has no omega, which is the point here; only that warning is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(mod, events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "omega"), events = events, ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
```

# Population

`r ui_wb$population$n_subjects` critically ill children with multiple organ
dysfunction syndrome (MODS) contributed `r ui_wb$population$n_observations`
whole-blood VAMS concentrations (Amajor 2026 Table 1). They were enrolled in
AMPLE, an ancillary antibiotic-PK cohort of the prospective observational
PARADIGM study, at 14 sites of the Pediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis
Investigators (PALISI) network. Children on continuous renal replacement
therapy or plasmapheresis were excluded; four (11%) were on ECMO.

* Age: median 10 years (range 1 month to 17 years); three were infants (1, 5
  and 5 months), all born at 37+ weeks.
* Weight: median 36 kg (4.3 to 213.6 kg); height median 135 cm.
* Female: 20 (54%).
* U25 eGFR at the start of sampling: median 87.37 mL/min/1.73 m^2
  (19.35 to 278.29); serum creatinine median 0.48 mg/dL.
* Illness severity: PELOD-2 median 6, PRISM III median 11, Proulx median 2;
  22 (59%) immunoparalysed (TNF-alpha response < 200 pg/mL).
* Dose: median 47.6 mg/kg per dose (9.4 to 54.3). The interval and infusion
  time are not reported.
* Sampling: up to 15 VAMS samples over 3 days, median 11 per child; none below
  the 0.1 mg/L limit of quantification.

The same information is in the models' `population` metadata
(`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Amajor_2026_cefepime_wholeblood"))$population`).

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Whole blood (`_wholeblood`) | Plasma (`_plasma`) | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` | log(5.14) L/h | log(2.97) L/h | Table 2 / Table 3, `CL (L/h)` |
| `lvc` | log(20.53) L | log(11.51) L | Table 2 / Table 3, `V1 (L)` |
| `lq` | log(0.64) L/h | log(0.46) L/h | Table 2 / Table 3, `Q (L/h)` |
| `lvp` | log(4.76) L | log(3.21) L | Table 2 / Table 3, `V2 (L)` |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.47 | 0.49 | Table 2 / Table 3, `theta GFR` |
| `e_age_vc` | -0.20 | -0.20 | Table 2 / Table 3, `theta Age` |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | 0.75 (fixed) | Table 2 / Table 3 equations; Methods, allometric powers 0.75 and 1 |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1 (fixed) | 1 (fixed) | Table 2 / Table 3 equations |
| `etalcl` | 0.38^2 = 0.1444 | 0.37^2 = 0.1369 | Table 2 / Table 3, `BSV CL` (footnote: reported as SD and CV%) |
| `etalvc` | 0.28^2 = 0.0784 | 0.29^2 = 0.0841 | Table 2 / Table 3, `BSV V1` |
| `propSd` | 0.25 | 0.25 (carried from Table 2) | Table 2, `RV`; Table 3 prints no RV row |
| No BSV on Q, V2 | -- | -- | Results, "PK model": fixed to zero |
| Reference WT 36 kg, eGFR 100, age 10 y | -- | -- | Table 2 / Table 3 equations |
| `cl`, `vc`, `q`, `vp` equations | -- | -- | Table 2 / Table 3 footers |
| Proportional error | -- | -- | Results, "PK model" |
| Whole-blood:plasma ratio 0.58 | -- | -- | Methods; Table S2 |

## Transcription check

Every row of Tables 2 and 3 prints an estimate, its standard error, its
relative standard error and a 95% interval. Those four numbers constrain one
another, so a misread digit shows up as an inconsistency.

```{r transcription-check}
tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,        ~parameter, ~value, ~se,   ~rse,  ~lo,   ~hi,   ~scale,
  "whole blood", "CL",        5.14,  0.33,  6.55,  4.53,  5.84,  "log",
  "whole blood", "V1",       20.53,  1.38,  6.72, 18.01, 23.41,  "log",
  "whole blood", "Q",         0.64,  0.31, 48.4,   0.28,  1.47,  "log",
  "whole blood", "V2",        4.76,  1.5,  31.5,   2.67,  8.48,  "log",
  "whole blood", "theta_GFR", 0.47,  0.043, 9.23,  0.38,  0.55,  "normal",
  "whole blood", "theta_Age", -0.20, 0.058, 28.5, -0.32, -0.09,  "normal",
  "whole blood", "BSV_CL",    0.38,  0.048, 12.7,  0.29,  0.48,  "log",
  "whole blood", "BSV_V1",    0.28,  0.054, 19.3,  0.19,  0.40,  "log",
  "whole blood", "RV",        0.25,  0.011,  4.21, 0.23,  0.27,  "normal",
  "plasma",      "CL",        2.97,  0.19,  6.48,  2.62,  3.37,  "log",
  "plasma",      "V1",       11.51,  0.93,  8.12,  9.83, 13.49,  "log",
  "plasma",      "Q",         0.46,  0.27, 57.8,   0.18,  1.20,  "log",
  "plasma",      "V2",        3.21,  0.89, 27.9,   1.91,  5.38,  "log",
  "plasma",      "theta_GFR", 0.49,  0.13, 26.0,   0.24,  0.74,  "normal",
  "plasma",      "theta_Age", -0.20, 0.06, 27.7,  -0.32, -0.09,  "normal",
  "plasma",      "BSV_CL",    0.37,  0.052, 13.9,  0.29,  0.49,  "log",
  "plasma",      "BSV_V1",    0.29,  0.065, 22.4,  0.19,  0.44,  "log"
) |>
  mutate(
    centre_from_ci = ifelse(scale == "log", sqrt(lo * hi), (lo + hi) / 2),
    ci_pct_diff = 100 * (centre_from_ci - value) / abs(value),
    se_from_rse = abs(value) * rse / 100,
    se_pct_diff = 100 * (se_from_rse - se) / se
  )

tab |>
  select(model, parameter, value, centre_from_ci, ci_pct_diff, se, se_from_rse, se_pct_diff) |>
  rename(
    "Model" = model,
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Printed value" = value,
    "Centre of printed CI" = centre_from_ci,
    "CI % diff" = ci_pct_diff,
    "Printed SE" = se,
    "SE from RSE" = se_from_rse,
    "SE % diff" = se_pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 3, 3, 1, 3, 3, 1))

# Deterministic arithmetic on transcribed numbers. The largest SE gap is
# plasma theta_Age (RSE 27.7% of 0.20 = 0.055, printed 0.06 after two-decimal
# rounding, -8%). The interval centre is looser because Monolix intervals are
# not exactly symmetric on either scale. A misread digit moves a value by tens
# of percent, so both bounds still go red on a transcription error.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(tab$se_pct_diff)) < 10,
  max(abs(tab$ci_pct_diff)) < 10
)
```

The theta-Age interval (-0.32 to -0.09) is centred on -0.205 in both tables,
matching the printed -0.20. The CV% printed beside each BSV standard deviation
is close to, but not exactly, `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)` (0.38 gives 39.4%
against the printed 39.0%; 0.28 gives 28.6% against 29.4%). The difference is
within the two-decimal rounding of omega, and the Results text quotes "39% BSV"
for CL and "28% BSV" for V1, so omega is read as a log-scale SD and squared.

# Verification against the published equations

## Covariate equations reproduced exactly

```{r covariate-equation-check}
grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  WT = c(4.3, 12, 36, 70, 213.6),
  CRCL = c(19.35, 87.37, 278.29),
  AGE = c(1 / 12, 5, 10, 17)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), time = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_)

eq_check <- function(mod, cl0, v10, q0, v20, th_gfr, th_age) {
  solve_typical(mod, grid, keep = c("WT", "CRCL", "AGE")) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(
      cl_eq = cl0 * (WT / 36)^0.75 * (CRCL / 100)^th_gfr,
      vc_eq = v10 * (WT / 36) * (AGE / 10)^th_age,
      q_eq = q0 * (WT / 36)^0.75,
      vp_eq = v20 * (WT / 36)
    ) |>
    summarise(
      cl = max(abs(cl / cl_eq - 1)), vc = max(abs(vc / vc_eq - 1)),
      q = max(abs(q / q_eq - 1)), vp = max(abs(vp / vp_eq - 1))
    )
}

eq_err <- bind_rows(
  `whole blood` = eq_check(mod_wb, 5.14, 20.53, 0.64, 4.76, 0.47, -0.20),
  plasma = eq_check(mod_pl, 2.97, 11.51, 0.46, 3.21, 0.49, -0.20),
  .id = "Model"
)
knitr::kable(eq_err, digits = 16, caption = "Maximum relative difference between the packaged typical-value parameters and the Table 2 / Table 3 equations evaluated by hand, over 60 covariate combinations spanning the cohort's ranges.")

# Same inputs on both sides, so only floating-point noise is possible.
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(eq_err[, -1]) < 1e-12))
```

## Numbers quoted in the Discussion

The Discussion evaluates the plasma model for two reference children. Both are
exact functions of the Table 3 equations.

```{r discussion-check}
typ_par <- function(mod, WT, CRCL, AGE) {
  solve_typical(
    mod,
    data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_,
               WT = WT, CRCL = CRCL, AGE = AGE)
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    select(cl, vc)
}

# 70 kg, eGFR 147 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (median of Morales Junior 2025): the paper
# quotes plasma CL 5.91 L/h and V1 22.4 L. The age-10 reference makes the age
# term 1, which is what the quoted V1 implies.
p70 <- typ_par(mod_pl, WT = 70, CRCL = 147, AGE = 10)
# 9 kg, eGFR 153 (median of de Cacqueray 2022): the paper quotes 1.05 L/h.
p9 <- typ_par(mod_pl, WT = 9, CRCL = 153, AGE = 10)
p9_no_gfr <- 2.97 * (9 / 36)^0.75

tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Plasma CL, 70 kg, eGFR 147", "Plasma V1, 70 kg, age 10",
               "Plasma CL, 9 kg, eGFR 153", "Plasma CL, 9 kg, eGFR term omitted"),
  `Packaged model` = c(p70$cl, p70$vc, p9$cl, p9_no_gfr),
  `Amajor 2026 Discussion` = c(5.91, 22.4, 1.05, 1.05)
) |>
  mutate(`% diff` = 100 * (`Packaged model` / `Amajor 2026 Discussion` - 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  abs(p70$cl / 5.91 - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(p70$vc / 22.4 - 1) < 0.005,
  # The 9-kg figure in the Discussion matches the equation only without its
  # eGFR term (see Assumptions and deviations); with the term it is 1.29 L/h.
  abs(p9_no_gfr / 1.05 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(p9$cl / 1.29 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

The 70-kg values reproduce to the printed precision. The 9-kg value of
1.05 L/h does not: the Table 3 equation gives 1.29 L/h at eGFR 153, and
1.05 L/h is what it gives with eGFR at the reference 100 (equivalently, with
the eGFR term left out). The packaged model follows the printed equation.

## The plasma re-fit tracks the 0.58 ratio

Dividing every observation by a constant should scale CL and the volumes by
that constant. The re-fit's CL ratio is 2.97 / 5.14 = 0.578, matching 0.58;
V1 (0.561), Q (0.72) and V2 (0.67) drift further, which is consistent with
their larger standard errors (Q and V2 have RSEs of 28-58%).

```{r ratio-check}
ratios <- c(CL = 2.97 / 5.14, V1 = 11.51 / 20.53, Q = 0.46 / 0.64, V2 = 3.21 / 4.76)
knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(Parameter = names(ratios), `Plasma / whole blood` = ratios), digits = 3)
stopifnot(abs(ratios[["CL"]] - 0.58) < 0.01)
```

# Virtual cohort

Individual data are not public. The cohort below is virtual: ages are drawn so
that the median is near the reported 10 years with a few infants, and weight
follows an approximate pooled-sex CDC 50th-percentile weight-for-age curve
with lognormal scatter (CV about 30%), wide enough to reach the obese tail the
cohort contains. U25 eGFR is lognormal around the reported median of
87 mL/min/1.73 m^2, truncated to the reported range. These distributions are
**assumptions of this vignette**, not published quantities.

Dosing is 50 mg/kg (capped at 2 g) every 8 hours as a 30-minute infusion. The
paper reports only the dose per kilogram (median 47.6, range 9.4 to 54.3
mg/kg); the minimum of 9.4 mg/kg is exactly a 2 g cap in the 213.6-kg child
(2000 / 213.6 = 9.36), which supports the cap.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261113)
n_sub <- 200L

# Approximate CDC 50th-percentile weight-for-age, sexes pooled (kg).
cdc_age <- c(1 / 12, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 17)
cdc_wt <- c(4.5, 7.8, 10, 12.5, 16.5, 20.7, 25.6, 32, 40.5, 50, 58, 61)

cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  AGE = pmax(17 * stats::rbeta(n_sub, 1.4, 1.0), 1 / 12),
  WT = pmin(pmax(
    stats::approx(cdc_age, cdc_wt, xout = AGE)$y * stats::rlnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.3),
    4.3
  ), 213.6),
  CRCL = pmin(pmax(stats::rlnorm(n_sub, log(87), 0.45), 19.35), 278.29),
  dose = pmin(50 * WT, 2000)
)

tau <- 8
t_inf <- 0.5
dose_times <- seq(0, 64, by = tau) # 9 doses, 0-72 h
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 72, by = 0.25), t_inf)))

ev <- bind_rows(
  cohort |> tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central", amt = dose, rate = dose / t_inf),
  cohort |> tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, rate, evid, cmt, WT, CRCL, AGE)

knitr::kable(
  cohort |> summarise(
    `Age median (y)` = median(AGE), `Infants (<1 y)` = sum(AGE < 1),
    `WT median (kg)` = median(WT), `WT range` = sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", min(WT), max(WT)),
    `eGFR median` = median(CRCL), `Dose median (mg/kg)` = median(dose / WT)
  ),
  digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort. Amajor 2026 Table 1: age 10 y (1 m-17 y), weight 36 kg (4.3-213.6), U25 eGFR 87.37 (19.35-278.29), dose 47.6 mg/kg (9.4-54.3)."
)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim_wb <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_wb, events = ev, keep = c("WT", "CRCL", "AGE")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(matrix = "whole blood (VAMS)")
sim_pl <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pl, events = ev, keep = c("WT", "CRCL", "AGE")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(matrix = "plasma-equivalent")
sim <- bind_rows(sim_wb, sim_pl)
stopifnot(all(c("id", "time", "Cc") %in% names(sim)))
```

## Concentration-time profiles

```{r profiles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  group_by(matrix, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = matrix, fill = matrix)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Cefepime (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles, 200 virtual children, 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) q8h, 30-min infusion."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Figure 3: visual predictive check

Figure 3 of Amajor 2026 is a prediction-corrected VPC of the whole-blood model
against time after the last dose, under the cohort's real (unreported)
regimens. The observed median line below was read approximately off that
figure by the maintainers; it is shown for orientation, against the simulated
whole-blood distribution over the third day (48-72 h) of the assumed regimen.
Prediction correction and the different regimens mean the two are not strictly
comparable.

```{r fig3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
fig3_obs_median <- tibble::tribble(
  ~tad, ~conc,
  1.0, 62,
  2.4, 45,
  4.2, 25,
  7.5, 12
)

vpc <- sim_wb |>
  filter(time >= 48, time < 72) |>
  mutate(tad = (time - 48) %% tau) |>
  group_by(tad) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = fig3_obs_median, aes(tad, conc), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Whole-blood cefepime (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 3 of Amajor 2026. Band: simulated 5th-95th percentiles.\nCrosses: observed median, read approximately from Figure 3."
  )

# Centre check on the TYPICAL-VALUE solve (etas zero), so it depends only
# on the R-seeded covariates and not on rxode2's per-thread eta stream: the
# median concentration 4.25 h after a day-3 dose is within a factor of 1.75 of
# the observed median read off Figure 3. Wide on purpose (the regimen is
# assumed and the figure is prediction-corrected); a clearance or volume
# mis-scaled by the 0.58 whole-blood:plasma factor moves it out.
typ_wb <- solve_typical(mod_wb, ev) |> as.data.frame()
med_4h <- typ_wb |>
  filter(abs(time - (48 + 4.25)) < 1e-8 | abs(time - (56 + 4.25)) < 1e-8 |
    abs(time - (64 + 4.25)) < 1e-8) |>
  pull(Cc) |>
  median()
cat(sprintf("Typical-value median 4.25 h after a day-3 dose: %.1f mg/L (Figure 3, about 25 mg/L)\n", med_4h))
stopifnot(med_4h / 25 > 1 / 1.75, med_4h / 25 < 1.75)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. PKNCA is used here to check what the two models
must agree on: the same dose to the same child should give a plasma AUC about
1 / 0.58 = 1.72 times the whole-blood AUC, because plasma CL is 0.58 times
whole-blood CL (with eGFR exponents 0.49 vs 0.47, the ratio drifts by under
3% across the eGFR range).

```{r pknca}
sim_typ <- bind_rows(
  solve_typical(mod_wb, ev, keep = c("WT", "CRCL", "AGE")) |>
    as.data.frame() |> mutate(matrix = "whole blood"),
  solve_typical(mod_pl, ev, keep = c("WT", "CRCL", "AGE")) |>
    as.data.frame() |> mutate(matrix = "plasma")
)

conc_df <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, matrix)
# The first infusion starts at t = 0, so the pre-dose concentration is 0.
conc_df <- bind_rows(conc_df, conc_df |> distinct(id, matrix) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
  distinct(id, matrix, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(matrix, id, time)

dose_df <- ev |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt) |>
  tidyr::crossing(matrix = c("whole blood", "plasma"))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | matrix + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | matrix + id, doseu = "mg")
# Cmin only for the ninth interval: over the first interval it is the
# pre-dose zero.
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 64), end = c(8, 72),
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE), auclast = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  mutate(interval = ifelse(start == 0, "first dose (0-8 h)", "ninth dose (64-72 h)"))

nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(matrix, interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "Interval" = interval,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin, "AUC (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median typical-value NCA over the virtual cohort.")

auc_ratio <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", interval == "ninth dose (64-72 h)") |>
  select(id, matrix, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = matrix, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(ratio = plasma / `whole blood`)

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    `Median plasma / whole-blood AUC` = median(auc_ratio$ratio),
    `Range` = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(auc_ratio$ratio), max(auc_ratio$ratio)),
    `Expected (1 / 0.58)` = 1 / 0.58
  ),
  digits = 3
)

# Typical values on both sides (no etas), so this is deterministic for a
# given cohort. The range reflects the V1/Q/V2 drift and the eGFR exponent
# difference, both bounded.
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_ratio) == n_sub,
  abs(median(auc_ratio$ratio) * 0.58 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Target attainment (paper Results)

For the 32 children who started cefepime at or after MODS onset, the paper
simulated each child's first 24 h of whole-blood exposure from the empirical
Bayes estimates and real doses, converted to free concentration assuming 20%
protein binding, and counted how many stayed above each MIC for the whole 24 h
(100% fT>MIC): 97% at 2 mg/L, 72% at 4, 41% at 8 and 9% at 16 mg/L.

The same calculation on the virtual cohort is below, using individual
predictions (`Cc`, no residual error) of the whole-blood model and the minimum
free concentration from the end of the first infusion to 24 h.

```{r pta}
min_free <- sim_wb |>
  filter(time >= t_inf, time <= 24) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(min_free = min(0.8 * Cc), .groups = "drop")

pta <- tibble::tibble(
  MIC = c(2, 4, 8, 16),
  `Amajor 2026 (%)` = c(97, 72, 41, 9)
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(`Virtual cohort (%)` = 100 * mean(min_free$min_free > MIC)) |>
  ungroup()
knitr::kable(pta, digits = 0, caption = "100% fT>MIC over the first 24 h, free concentration = 0.8 x whole-blood concentration.")
cat(sprintf("Median minimum free concentration, 0.5-24 h: %.1f mg/L\n", median(min_free$min_free)))

# Centre, not tails, and on the typical-value solve so it does not depend on
# rxode2's eta stream: the paper's 50% crossing lies between MIC 4 (72%) and
# 8 mg/L (41%). Under the assumed regimen and cohort, the median of the
# typical-value minimum free concentration should fall in a band around that
# (3-15 mg/L); a clearance mis-scaled by the 0.58 factor moves it out.
min_free_typ <- typ_wb |>
  filter(time >= t_inf, time <= 24) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(min_free = min(0.8 * Cc), .groups = "drop")
cat(sprintf("Typical-value median minimum free concentration, 0.5-24 h: %.1f mg/L\n", median(min_free_typ$min_free)))
stopifnot(
  nrow(min_free_typ) == n_sub,
  median(min_free_typ$min_free) > 3,
  median(min_free_typ$min_free) < 15
)
```

The virtual cohort reaches each target more often than the study children
did. The doses and intervals the children actually received are not reported,
and attainment of 100% fT>MIC depends strongly on the dosing interval, so this
gap is expected under an assumed q8h regimen. It is also lighter than the
study cohort (median `r round(median(cohort$WT))` kg against 36 kg) and lacks its heaviest children.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two models, one fit.** The plasma model is the authors' re-run of the
  final whole-blood model on VAMS concentrations divided by 0.58. No plasma
  sample was assayed in these patients, and the 0.58 ratio comes from in vitro
  spiked blood (30 paired samples over 0.2 to 150 mg/L; Table S2). The paper
  notes that clinical validation of the ratio is still needed.
* **Residual error of the plasma model is carried over.** Table 3 prints no
  RV row. Dividing every observation by the same constant leaves a
  proportional residual unchanged, so the whole-blood value of 0.25 is used.
* **The 9-kg comparison in the Discussion does not match the equation.** The
  Discussion states a plasma CL of 1.05 L/h for a 9-kg child with eGFR
  153 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The Table 3 equation gives 1.29 L/h; 1.05 L/h is the
  value with the eGFR term at its reference. The 70-kg comparison in the same
  paragraph matches the equation exactly, so the equation is taken as
  correct.
* **BSV is read as a log-scale SD.** Tables 2 and 3 say "BSV reported as SD
  and CV%". The printed CV% values are within rounding of the lognormal
  conversion.
* **eGFR is time-varying in the source.** The paper updated U25 eGFR daily and
  interpolated between values in Monolix. The vignette holds it constant per
  child. Users with daily creatinine should supply a time-varying `CRCL`
  column.
* **The CKiD U25 equation is not in the model.** It is applied when preparing
  `CRCL`, using serum creatinine only (the highest value of each day), as the
  paper did. eGFR from another equation, such as bedside Schwartz, rescales the
  renal term.
* **Age must be positive.** The age effect is a power function centred on 10
  years. Infant ages go in as fractional years.
* **Dosing is assumed.** The paper reports the dose per kilogram only. The
  vignette uses 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) q8h as a 30-minute infusion, so its
  comparisons with the published target attainment and Figure 3 are
  consistency checks, not reproductions.
* **Protein binding is the paper's assumption.** The 20% binding applied to
  whole-blood concentrations for fT>MIC follows the paper. Protein binding is
  a plasma property, so this is an approximation for whole blood.
* **Covariate screen.** Covariates screened and not kept are listed in the
  model files' `covariatesDataExcluded` (PELOD-2, Proulx, fluid status, ECMO)
  and in the `population` notes (Table S4).
* **Figures 1 and 2 are not reproduced.** Figure 1 is a sampling schematic
  and Figure 2 is a set of goodness-of-fit plots that need the observed data.
